Fixed in nidaq.py: DO now uses one single-line task per valve (keyed by valve key) instead of one multi-line task per module, so a write touches only its own line. write_do/_flush_do/_ensure_do_task/_close_sync updated. Verified against the real backend code with an injected fake nidaqmx: opening ar_pneumatic then pulsing rpm_top (same module) 4x leaves ar open, one task per valve, scalar writes. Logic-complete; NOT yet live on the running server (needs a restart, which drops output lines low) and still wants a bench check that two valves on one module drive independently on real hardware.

Fixed: valve_state is now persisted to config/valve_state.json on every set_valve call and reloaded at Supervisor init (falls back to False for unknown valves). Restore only updates the in-memory model - never writes to hardware, keeping connect/restart read-only. Verified with a two-Supervisor repro (simulated restart): state survives, and the restore step made zero hardware writes. Also corrected a false assumption in stop()'s docstring and docs/CONTROL_MODEL.md claiming DAQmx resets lines low on task close - contradicted by the Ar valve staying open across a restart. Seeded config/valve_state.json with the live server's current model (plasma_ground open, rest closed) before this fix's first restart, so that transition doesn't repeat the bug.

Implemented: MfcCfg gained isolation_valve (config/reactor.yaml: ar -> ar_pneumatic). set_mfc_setpoint refuses sccm>0 while the isolation valve is closed (ValueError/409); set_valve auto-zeros any MFC whose isolation_valve was just closed. UI: MFC tile shows a note and disables Set Flow while the valve is closed. Verified against real Supervisor code with a fake DAQ+MFC: refused while closed, accepted at 5 sccm once opened, auto-zeroed on close.

Reignite defaults tightened 0.5/1.0s -> 0.10/0.15s (Step model + build_ald_recipe), now exposed as two ALD-run UI fields with a live achieved-rate hint (accounts for the loop's 0.2s poll, not just pulse+settle). Verified against real recipe.py: single _reignite() 3.8/s; full electron_beam retry loop under continuous no-plasma conditions measured 2.14/s (>=2/s target). Chart fix: reignite is two valve commands (pulse-on then beam-back-on); only the beam-back-on transition (state===false) now draws the red retry marker, the interrupt pulse draws nothing.

Implemented and verified live against the running server (not yet restarted onto the faster-polling backend, but frontend confirmed rendering real flow data at current 2Hz cadence with no console errors).

Implemented per the design agreed in chat, with the operator's tweak: two independent lead times, not one - 'first' gas lead_s is wall-clock seconds before beam start (precomputed once/cycle from fixed dose_s+pump_a_s); 'second' gas lead_s is exposure-seconds before the computed handoff point, evaluated live against the same lit-exposure accumulator the reignite loop already freezes during a reignite or operator pause, so the handoff inherits that freeze for free (verified: forcing one reignite mid-window shifted the handoff exactly by the dead time, not on a fixed wall-clock schedule). New GasSchedule model (mfc/order/pct/flow_sccm/lead_s) on Recipe; build_ald_recipe validates at most one 'first' and one 'second'; scheduled gases zeroed in setup and (already) at run end. UI: Gas scheduling table in the ALD panel (enable/order/%/flow/lead per gas) with a live plain-English timeline matching the exact backend math, verified byte-for-byte against a 3-scenario fake-supervisor test run against the real RecipeRunner code. Also added: run-parameter snapshot (DataLogger.write_ald_snapshot) - a JSON sidecar written at every ALD run start with the full built Recipe (cycles, phase timings, gas schedule) plus the raw UI params plus a human-readable summary, independent of whether the tab-delimited logger is running.

Stage bias confirmed working by Zach 2026-08-25 after the read-back + wider event window shipped. Root cause never pinned down: the parameter always reached the device (the voltage setpoint moved 20 -> 30 V, which only pre-start's set_voltage does), so the failure was at set_output or below, but the pre-start events had scrolled out of the 40-event window before they could be read. supplies_output_on now reads the output back and raises an explicit ERROR event if the supply still reports OFF after being commanded ON, so a recurrence will say so plainly. Reopen if it comes back. The other three issues in this bead were root-caused and fixed: Tailscale trend seeding (/api/trend was never fetched), the save dialog firing on every connected client, and the asyncio socket.send WARNING spam.

Superseded and REMOVED the same day it shipped. The restart re-exec'd the process; on 2026-08-25 an old instance survived it, so two servers ran at once - the newer holding port 8000 while the older still held COM8-COM12 - and every device looked unreachable. Zach: 'I don't need a restart, really, just a button that kills all servers in use.' Replaced by Diagnostics > Shut down server, which kills sibling reactor processes first, then tears itself down through the normal lifespan teardown and calls os._exit(0). See reactor-tp1/reactor-799 notes and docs/CONTROL_MODEL.md. KEY LESSON KEPT: main() returning does NOT end the process - a non-daemon thread keeps it alive, which is exactly how that orphan survived holding its serial ports.
